beats.care: You can now check your candidate's affidavit and act if something looks false. Real power for voters.
beats.what: The Supreme Court said ordinary citizens, not just officials, can file complaints against candidates who lie in their poll affidavits.
beats.why: Affidavits list a candidate's assets, education and criminal cases. Lying in them is an offence, but it was unclear who could complain.

cards.body: Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said Section 125-A of the Representation of the People Act lets courts act even on a private person's complaint.
Or a fine, or both, under Section 125-A.
cards.caption: Maximum jail for a false affidavit

cards.body: The court said if lawmakers wanted only officials to complain, they would have changed the law. They didn't.

cards.q: Would you check your candidate's affidavit before voting?
Who can now file a case over a false nomination affidavit?
cards.why: The SC said any private citizen has the right to file a complaint under Section 125-A.

hook: A neta lied in his poll papers? Now *you* can take him to court

learn.t: Candidates' affidavits, with assets and criminal cases, are public on the Election Commission's website.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: SC backs voters' right to prosecute candidates (print, Hyderabad edition, 24 Oct, p.11)

tldr: The Supreme Court ruled that any voter can file a criminal case against a candidate who hides or fakes details in nomination papers.
watch: Watch whether this leads to more cases against candidates in the next round of State elections.
